title: Three same readings
prompt: Show the different temp_c values that appear in at least 3 consecutive readings, ordering all readings by id.
hints: Compare with the two previous rows.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE readings SET temp_c = 9 WHERE id IN (2, 3, 4); UPDATE readings SET temp_c = 5 WHERE id IN (1, 6, 8);

solutions: SELECT DISTINCT temp_c FROM (SELECT temp_c, LAG(temp_c, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS p1, LAG(temp_c, 2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS p2 FROM readings) WHERE temp_c = p1 AND temp_c = p2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT temp_c FROM (SELECT temp_c, LAG(temp_c, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS p1 FROM readings) WHERE temp_c = p1;
wrongSolutions.why: Needs only two in a row

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT temp_c FROM readings GROUP BY temp_c HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
wrongSolutions.why: Doesn't require them to be consecutive

title: Stock limit
prompt: Order items are packed by order_id, then product_id. A box holds 5 units. Show the order_id and product_id of the last item that fits in the box without going over.
hints: A running SUM with a unique order.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, product_id FROM (SELECT order_id, product_id, SUM(quantity) OVER (ORDER BY order_id, product_id) AS packed FROM order_items) WHERE packed <= 5 ORDER BY packed DESC, order_id DESC, product_id DESC LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, product_id FROM order_items WHERE quantity <= 5 ORDER BY order_id DESC, product_id DESC LIMIT 1;

SELECT order_id, product_id FROM (SELECT order_id, product_id, SUM(quantity) OVER (ORDER BY order_id, product_id) AS packed FROM order_items) WHERE packed <= 5 ORDER BY packed, order_id, product_id LIMIT 1;

title: Three-day average minutes
prompt: First total minutes per date. Then show each session_date, its 3-calendar-day total as total, and that total divided by 3, rounded to 2 decimals, as average. Skip the first 2 calendar days after the earliest date.
hints: Filter dates at least 2 days after the first.
solutions: WITH d AS (SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS day_total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date) SELECT session_date, total, ROUND(total / 3.0, 2) AS average FROM (SELECT session_date, SUM(day_total) OVER (ORDER BY julianday(session_date) RANGE BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM d) WHERE julianday(session_date) >= (SELECT MIN(julianday(session_date)) + 2 FROM d) ORDER BY session_date;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS day_total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date) SELECT session_date, SUM(day_total) OVER (ORDER BY julianday(session_date) RANGE BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total, 0 AS average FROM d ORDER BY session_date;
SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS total, ROUND(SUM(minutes) / 3.0, 2) AS average FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY session_date;

title: Top scorers per course
prompt: Show the course title, student name, and grade for students with one of the top 2 different grades in each course. Ties all count, and ungraded enrolments don't.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 7, 5, 60, '2024-autumn'), (16, 8, 5, 50, '2024-autumn');

solutions: SELECT title, name, grade FROM (SELECT c.title, s.name, e.grade, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY e.grade DESC) AS r FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL) WHERE r <= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, name, grade FROM (SELECT c.title, s.name, e.grade, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY e.grade DESC) AS r FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL) WHERE r <= 2;

SELECT title, name, grade FROM (SELECT c.title, s.name, e.grade, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY e.grade DESC) AS r FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL) WHERE r <= 2;
wrongSolutions.why: A tie for first skips the second level
